theory.overview: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) is the mathematical brain of every processor. It performs all arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction) and logical operations (AND, OR, comparison) that make computation possible. At its core sits the adder—a deceptively simple circuit that, when combined with clever logic, enables complex mathematics. Understanding how adders work reveals the elegance of computer design: from a single full adder handling one bit, to cascaded ripple-carry adders, to sophisticated carry-lookahead designs that power modern CPUs.

sections.title: The Half Adder: Starting Simple
sections.content: The simplest adder handles just two bits, producing a sum and carry. The sum is computed with XOR (outputs 1 when inputs differ), and the carry is computed with AND (outputs 1 only when both are 1). This is called a 'half' adder because it doesn't account for a carry-in from a previous bit—making it suitable only for the least significant bit position.

sections.title: The Full Adder: Complete Addition
sections.content: Real addition needs to handle carries from previous positions. The full adder takes three inputs: A, B, and Carry-in (Cin). It produces Sum and Carry-out (Cout). The full adder can be built from two half adders plus an OR gate for the carry logic. This is the fundamental building block for multi-bit addition.

equations.Cout: (A AND B) OR (Cin AND (A XOR B))

sections.implementation: Two half adders + one OR gate

sections.title: Ripple-Carry Adder: Chaining Together
sections.content: To add multi-bit numbers, connect full adders in a chain where each carry-out becomes the next carry-in. This is called a ripple-carry adder—simple but slow. The worst-case delay is proportional to the number of bits because the carry must 'ripple' through every stage. A 32-bit ripple-carry adder needs 32 full-adder delays.

sections.title: Carry-Lookahead Adder: Speed at Cost
sections.content: Modern CPUs can't wait for carries to ripple. Carry-lookahead adders (CLA) compute carry bits in parallel using generate (G = A AND B) and propagate (P = A XOR B) signals. If G=1, a carry is definitely generated. If P=1, a carry-in will propagate through. This allows computing all carries simultaneously, reducing delay to O(log n) but requiring more gates.

sections.title: Subtraction via Addition
sections.content: Subtraction A - B is implemented as A + (-B). In two's complement, -B is computed as NOT(B) + 1. So A - B = A + NOT(B) + 1. This means the same adder hardware can do subtraction—we just invert B and set the initial carry-in to 1. This elegant design eliminates the need for separate subtraction circuits.
steps: Invert all bits of B (one's complement)
Add A to the complemented B

sections.title: The ALU: Beyond Addition
sections.content: A complete ALU performs arithmetic (ADD, SUB) and logic (AND, OR, NOT, XOR) operations. A control signal selects which operation to perform. The ALU also outputs status flags: Zero (result is zero), Negative (MSB is 1), Carry (overflow from addition), and Overflow (signed overflow). These flags enable conditional branching in programs.

keyConcepts.name: Half Adder
keyConcepts.description: Adds two 1-bit inputs, produces 1-bit sum and 1-bit carry. No carry-in input.

keyConcepts.name: Full Adder
keyConcepts.description: Adds two 1-bit inputs plus 1-bit carry-in. Produces sum and carry-out.

keyConcepts.name: Ripple Delay
keyConcepts.description: The time for a carry to propagate through all bits. Limits maximum clock speed.

keyConcepts.name: Generate/Propagate
keyConcepts.description: Signals used in fast adders. Generate: definitely creates carry. Propagate: passes carry through.

complexity.carryLookahead: O(log n) delay, O(n log n) gates

practiceProblems.description: What are Sum and Carry when adding 1 + 1 in a half adder?

practiceProblems.title: Full Adder with Carry
practiceProblems.description: In a full adder, A=1, B=0, Cin=1. What is Sum?
practiceProblems.explanation: Sum = A XOR B XOR Cin = 1 XOR 0 XOR 1 = 0. (1⊕0=1, then 1⊕1=0).

practiceProblems.title: 4-bit Addition
practiceProblems.explanation: 6 + 3 = 9. Binary: 0110 + 0011 = 1001. Carries flow from right to left.
hints: Add bit by bit from right

practiceProblems.title: Subtraction Using Adder
practiceProblems.description: To subtract B from A using an adder, what must be done to B?
practiceProblems.explanation: A - B = A + (-B) = A + NOT(B) + 1. Two's complement negation.

practiceProblems.title: Ripple-Carry Delay
practiceProblems.description: If each full adder has 2ns delay, what's the total delay for a 32-bit ripple-carry adder?
practiceProblems.explanation: 32 stages × 2ns per stage = 64ns. The carry must ripple through all bits.
hints: Delay is proportional to bit width

practiceProblems.title: Generate and Propagate
practiceProblems.description: When does a bit position generate a carry in a CLA?
practiceProblems.answer: When both A and B are 1
practiceProblems.explanation: G = A AND B. Generate means this position definitely creates a carry regardless of Cin.

snippets.title: Adder Simulation
snippets.code:
# Half Adder
def half_adder(a, b):
    sum_bit = a ^ b
    carry = a & b
    return sum_bit, carry

# Full Adder
def full_adder(a, b, cin):
    sum1, carry1 = half_adder(a, b)
    sum_out, carry2 = half_adder(sum1, cin)
    carry_out = carry1 | carry2
    return sum_out, carry_out

# N-bit Ripple-Carry Adder
def n_bit_adder(a_bits, b_bits, n):
    result = []
    carry = 0
    for i in range(n):
        s, carry = full_adder(a_bits[i], b_bits[i], carry)
        result.append(s)
    return result, carry  # carry is overflow

# Test: 5 + 3 = 8
a = [1, 0, 1, 0]  # 5 = 0101 (LSB first)
b = [1, 1, 0, 0]  # 3 = 0011
sum_bits, cout = n_bit_adder(a, b, 4)
print(f'5 + 3 = {sum_bits} with carry {cout}')  # 1000 = 8

# Convert to decimal for verification
def bits_to_dec(bits):
    return sum(b << i for i, b in enumerate(bits))
print(f'Result: {bits_to_dec(sum_bits)}')
